findings.title: Continue from QR screen submits an empty TOTP code
findings.body: The `goto-otp-screen` button has `type="submit"` inside the `Form` whose submit handler is `handleEnable`, and its `onClick` only calls `setStep(SetupStep.EnterTotpCode)` without calling `preventDefault`. Clicking "Continue" on the QR step therefore immediately invokes `handleEnable` before the user has entered a TOTP code, causing an API request with an empty/missing code and an incorrect-code error on the next screen. This should be `type="button"` or the click handler should call `e.preventDefault()`.

findings.title: Closing the backup-code dialog via X/backdrop skips onEnable
findings.body: After 2FA is enabled, `onEnable` is only invoked by the `backup-codes-close` button. The `Dialog` can also be closed with its X button, backdrop, or Escape, which only uses `onOpenChange`. If the user closes the backup-code screen through one of those paths instead of clicking "Close", `onEnable` never runs, so the parent settings page can remain in the pre-enable state even though 2FA is already enabled in the database. Either call `onEnable` immediately after successful enable or ensure every close path from the final screen invokes it.

findings.title: Backup codes are consumed non-atomically
findings.body: The backup code is checked with `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` on the selected array, then a separate Prisma update re-encrypts and stores the modified array. There is no transaction, conditional update, or deletion of the specific code in the database. If the same valid backup code is submitted in concurrent login requests before one request updates the stored codes, both requests can pass the `indexOf` check and both can be authorized, breaking the one-time-use guarantee for backup codes.

findings.title: No e2e coverage for backup-code login or disable
findings.body: The added test only checks download, copy, and close on the backup-code screen after enabling 2FA. The central security-sensitive paths introduced by this PR — logging in with a backup code, disabling 2FA with a backup code, and ensuring a used backup code cannot be reused — are not tested. The TODO at line 12 acknowledges this gap, but these paths are currently where regressions would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle is no longer keyboard accessible
findings.body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide password button removes it from the keyboard tab order. Keyboard and assistive-technology users can no longer focus or activate the toggle, while mouse users are unaffected. Unless there is an alternative accessible control for this action, this is an accessibility regression and should be reverted or given an accessible keyboard handler.
